<header class="dg-head dg-head-chapter"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 7</p><h1 class="dg-title">Metric</h1></header>
<div class="dg-motivation"><div class="dg-motivation-title">Motivation: Distances, geodesics, and the variational principle</div><div class="dg-motivation-upper"><p>A connection decides which curves are straight, but not how long they are, nor the angle between two vectors. On <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^d\)</span>, in Cartesian coordinates, the length of a curve is computed from the components of its velocity,  <span class="math display">\[
        L_{[a,b]}[\gamma] = \int_a^b \sqrt{ \delta_{ij} \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) } \; d\lambda ,
    \]</span>  i.e. by evaluating the Euclidean inner product <span class="math inline">\(\delta_{ij}\)</span> on the velocity <span class="math inline">\(v_{\gamma(\lambda)}\)</span> at every <span class="math inline">\(\lambda\)</span>. On a manifold, the velocity <span class="math inline">\(v_{\gamma(\lambda)} \in T_{\gamma(\lambda)}\mathcal{M}\)</span> is available (Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Tangent_Spaces">4</a>), but nothing yet turns it into a number: a tangent space is a vector space, with no lengths or angles, and the components <span class="math inline">\(\delta_{ij}\)</span> only take this form in Cartesian charts. The missing ingredient is a symmetric, non-degenerate bilinear form on every tangent space, varying smoothly from point to point. Positive definiteness is not required, so that the Lorentzian case, the one of spacetime, is included.</p>
</div><div class="dg-motivation-lower">
<p><strong>Goal:</strong> construct this structure and relate it to the connection.</p>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>Define the <strong>metric</strong> <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span>, whose components <span class="math inline">\(g_{ij}\)</span> replace <span class="math inline">\(\delta_{ij}\)</span>, and classify it by its signature.</p></li>
<li><p>Define the length of curves and, as its extremal curves, the <strong>geodesics</strong>, using <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> alone, independently of any connection.</p></li>
<li><p>Single out a connection whose straight curves are the geodesics: the Levi-Civita connection <span class="math inline">\(\nabla^{\text{LC}}\)</span>, determined by <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span>, and characterized as the only torsion-free, metric-compatible connection.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>In general relativity, <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> is the gravitational field, and the curvatures of <span class="math inline">\(\nabla^{\text{LC}}\)</span>, built from <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> at the end of this chapter, are the objects entering the Einstein equations.</p></div></div>
